Ui.Script:
-- ── Strings (GlobalStrings.lua, verbatim; line numbers cited) ─────────────────────────── -- `X = X or "…"` throughout, FriendsFrame.xml's rule: several of these are names the real -- string table already owns, and in a live session it has already run. RAID = RAID or "Raid" -- l.3256 RAID_DESCRIPTION = RAID_DESCRIPTION or "Raids are groups of more than 5 people and are typically used to defeat unique challenges at high levels.\n\n|cffffffff- Raid members cannot earn credit toward most non-raid quests. Specifically, they will not receive non-raid quest credit for killing creatures or collecting items.\n\n- Raids grant substantially less experience for defeating monsters than normal groups.\n\n- Raids allow you to overcome challenges that might otherwise be nearly impossible.|r" -- l.3262 CONVERT_TO_RAID = CONVERT_TO_RAID or "Convert To Raid" -- l.863 RAID_INFO = RAID_INFO or "Raid Info" -- l.3264 RAID_INFORMATION = RAID_INFORMATION or "Raid Information" -- l.3265 RAID_INFO_DESC = RAID_INFO_DESC or "Your saved raid instance status." -- l.3266 RESETS_IN = RESETS_IN or "Resets in" -- l.3341 INSTANCE = INSTANCE or "INSTANCE" -- l.2331 ID = ID or "ID" -- l.2303 ADD_RAID_MEMBER = ADD_RAID_MEMBER or "Add Member" -- l.40 ADD_RAIDMEMBER_LABEL = ADD_RAIDMEMBER_LABEL or "Add Raid Member:" -- l.39 READY_CHECK = READY_CHECK or "Ready Check" -- l.3301 READY_CHECK_MESSAGE = READY_CHECK_MESSAGE or "%s has initiated a ready check.\n|cffffffffAre you ready?|r" -- l.3302 READY_CHECK_YOU_WERE_AFK = READY_CHECK_YOU_WERE_AFK or "You were AFK for a ready check" -- l.3305 RAID_LEADER_TOKEN = RAID_LEADER_TOKEN or "(L)" -- l.3276 RAID_ASSISTANT_TOKEN = RAID_ASSISTANT_TOKEN or "(A)" -- l.3259 GROUP = GROUP or "Group" -- l.2029 EMPTY = EMPTY or "Empty" -- l.1433 UNKNOWN = UNKNOWN or "Unknown" -- l.4443
-- ── The counts (ref RaidFrame.lua l.2-5) ──────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Published globals, not local constants: `MAX_RAID_MEMBERS` alone is named by a large -- slice of the raid-addon corpus, which sweeps `1, MAX_RAID_MEMBERS` rather than -- `1, GetNumRaidMembers()` precisely so a shrinking roster still clears its stale rows. MAX_RAID_MEMBERS = 40 NUM_RAID_GROUPS = 8 MEMBERS_PER_RAID_GROUP = 5 MAX_RAID_INFOS = 10
-- The drag's two pieces of state, ref-named (l.2-3): the row currently under the cursor, -- and the slot it is hovering. Globals because the ref publishes them and because the -- pane's OnUpdate, its OnHide and the row's own handlers all three read them. MOVING_RAID_MEMBER = nil TARGET_RAID_SLOT = nil
-- `RAID_SUBGROUP_LISTS[subgroupNumber]` and `[classFileName]` — the row indices in each -- bucket, rebuilt on every repaint (ref l.4, filled in `RaidGroupFrame_Update`). Nothing -- in this file reads them: they are the PULLOUTS' input, and the pullouts are the stated -- deferral above. They are filled anyway because they are also the published surface a -- raid addon reads to answer "who is in group 3 / who are the priests" without walking the -- roster itself, and filling them is four lines inside a loop that already has the answer. RAID_SUBGROUP_LISTS = {}
local function set_shown(widget, on) if on then widget:Show() else widget:Hide() end end
local function set_enabled(widget, on) if on then widget:Enable() else widget:Disable() end end
-- ── The pane (ref RaidFrame_OnLoad l.7-27 / RaidFrame_OnEvent l.29-58) ────────────────── function RaidFrame_OnLoad() this:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_LOGIN") this:RegisterEvent("RAID_ROSTER_UPDATE") this:RegisterEvent("UPDATE_INSTANCE_INFO") this:RegisterEvent("PARTY_MEMBERS_CHANGED") this:RegisterEvent("PARTY_LEADER_CHANGED") this:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") -- The grid's two per-unit repaints (ref `RaidGroupFrame_OnLoad` l.9-10, which adds -- them to this same frame once the addon loads). They are what keeps a death or a -- ding off `RAID_ROSTER_UPDATE`. this:RegisterEvent("UNIT_LEVEL") this:RegisterEvent("UNIT_HEALTH") -- Ref l.26: the button is dead until the server has answered ONCE. `hasRaidInfo` is -- the ref's "the first UPDATE_INSTANCE_INFO is the seeding one" latch; see OnEvent. RaidFrame.hasRaidInfo = nil RaidFrame_Update() end
function RaidFrame_OnEvent(event) if event == "PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD" then RequestRaidInfo() end if event == "PLAYER_LOGIN" then if GetNumRaidMembers() > 0 then RaidFrame_Update() end end if event == "RAID_ROSTER_UPDATE" then RaidFrame_Update() end if event == "UPDATE_INSTANCE_INFO" then -- Ref l.42-48, transcribed including its shape: the FIRST answer only arms the -- latch and returns, so the button's state is decided from the second onward. The -- reference's reason is that its first `UPDATE_INSTANCE_INFO` fires before the -- data has landed; ours fires with the data, so the latch costs one extra -- `RequestRaidInfo` round trip and nothing else. Kept because an addon that -- watches `RaidFrame.hasRaidInfo` — several raid-lockout addons do — is watching a -- documented two-state field, and collapsing it to one state is a behaviour -- change we would be making silently. if not RaidFrame.hasRaidInfo then RaidFrame.hasRaidInfo = 1 return end set_enabled(RaidFrameRaidInfoButton, GetNumSavedInstances() > 0) RaidInfoFrame_Update() end if event == "PARTY_MEMBERS_CHANGED" or event == "PARTY_LEADER_CHANGED" then RaidFrame_Update() end end
-- Ref RaidFrame_Update l.60-78. Out of a raid the pane is the blurb and one button; in one -- it is the grid. The two are mutually exclusive, which is why nothing here reads both. function RaidFrame_Update() if GetNumRaidMembers() == 0 then RaidFrameConvertToRaidButton:Show() -- Ref l.64-68: convertible only with a party to convert AND the lead of it. -- `GetPartyMember(1)` rather than `GetNumPartyMembers() > 0` is the ref's own -- spelling, and they answer the same thing. set_enabled(RaidFrameConvertToRaidButton, GetPartyMember(1) and IsPartyLeader()) RaidFrameRaidDescription:Show() else RaidFrameConvertToRaidButton:Hide() RaidFrameRaidDescription:Hide() end -- Ref l.75-77 keeps this behind an existence test because the grid lives in a -- load-on-demand addon there. Ours is in this file, so the test always passes — kept -- verbatim anyway: an addon that replaces `RaidGroupFrame_Update` with nil to suppress -- the grid is relying on this guard, and the guard costs nothing. if RaidGroupFrame_Update then RaidGroupFrame_Update() end end
-- ── The grid (ref Blizzard_RaidUI.lua RaidGroupFrame_Update l.45-176) ─────────────────── function RaidGroupFrame_Update() local numRaidMembers = GetNumRaidMembers() for i = 1, NUM_RAID_GROUPS do local group = getglobal("RaidGroup" .. i) set_shown(group, numRaidMembers > 0) -- The fill cursor: which of this group's five slots the next member lands in. group.nextIndex = 1 end
RaidFrameReadyCheckButton_Update() RaidFrameAddMemberButton_Update() -- Ref l.60-62: Raid Info shares its row with Ready Check, so it steps aside when Ready -- Check is on screen. Only ever re-anchored one way — the ref never puts it back, -- because Ready Check showing and the raid existing are the same condition for the -- leader, and a non-leader never sees either. if RaidFrameReadyCheckButton:IsShown() then RaidFrameRaidInfoButton:SetPoint("LEFT", "RaidFrameReadyCheckButton", "RIGHT", 2, 0) end
RaidGroup_ResetSlotButtons()
-- Rebuild the published buckets (see RAID_SUBGROUP_LISTS above). One per subgroup, -- and one per CLASS token — the ref keys both into the same table, which is safe -- because subgroup keys are numbers and class keys are strings. RAID_SUBGROUP_LISTS = {} for i = 1, NUM_RAID_GROUPS do RAID_SUBGROUP_LISTS[i] = {} end for token in pairs(RAID_CLASS_COLORS) do RAID_SUBGROUP_LISTS[token] = {} end
for i = 1, MAX_RAID_MEMBERS do local button = getglobal("RaidGroupButton" .. i) if i <= numRaidMembers then local name, rank, subgroup, level, class, fileName, zone, online, isDead = GetRaidRosterInfo(i) local group = getglobal("RaidGroup" .. subgroup) -- Ref l.90's own comment: "To prevent errors when the server hiccups". A -- sixth member in a subgroup is not representable, so the row simply does not -- seat — better a missing row than an overlapping one. if group and group.nextIndex <= MEMBERS_PER_RAID_GROUP then button.id = i button.name = name button.unit = "raid" .. i button.class = fileName button.subgroup = subgroup
RaidGroupButton_SetRow(button, name, rank, level, class, fileName, online, isDead)
table.insert(RAID_SUBGROUP_LISTS[subgroup], i) if fileName and RAID_SUBGROUP_LISTS[fileName] then table.insert(RAID_SUBGROUP_LISTS[fileName], i) end
local slotName = "RaidGroup" .. subgroup .. "Slot" .. group.nextIndex -- Ref l.160: the row being DRAGGED keeps the cursor, not its slot — the -- repaint must not yank it out from under the hand holding it. if MOVING_RAID_MEMBER ~= button then button:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", slotName, "TOPLEFT", 0, 0) end -- Both directions of the row<->slot link: the row remembers where to -- spring back to on a cancelled drag, the slot remembers who is in it so -- a drop onto an occupied slot knows to SWAP rather than to move. button.slot = slotName getglobal(slotName).button = button:GetName() group.nextIndex = group.nextIndex + 1 button:SetID(i) button:Show() else button:Hide() end else button:Hide() end end end
-- One row's text and colour (ref l.96-152, lifted out of the sweep above so the two -- per-unit event handlers below can reuse the colour half without repainting everything). function RaidGroupButton_SetRow(button, name, rank, level, class, fileName, online, isDead) local prefix = button:GetName() if level == 0 then level = "" end if not name then name = UNKNOWN end getglobal(prefix .. "Name"):SetText(name) getglobal(prefix .. "Class"):SetText(class or "") getglobal(prefix .. "Level"):SetText(level or "") -- The rank tokens (ref l.146-152): "(L)" for the leader, "(A)" for an assistant. local token = "" if rank == 2 then token = RAID_LEADER_TOKEN elseif rank == 1 then token = RAID_ASSISTANT_TOKEN end getglobal(prefix .. "Rank"):SetText(token) RaidGroupButton_SetRowColor(button, fileName, online, isDead) end
-- The colour law, ONE function because the reference repeats it twice verbatim -- (`RaidGroupFrame_Update` l.130-145 and `RaidGroupFrame_UpdateHealth` l.184-199) and the -- two must never disagree: offline is grey and wins over everything, then dead is red, -- then the class colour. All three columns take the same colour together. function RaidGroupButton_SetRowColor(button, fileName, online, isDead) local prefix = button:GetName() local color if not online then color = GRAY_FONT_COLOR elseif isDead then color = RED_FONT_COLOR else color = RAID_CLASS_COLORS[fileName] end -- A class with no colour (an unresolved row) leaves the columns as they were, which is -- the reference's own behaviour: its `if ( color )` guard skips the write rather than -- falling back to white. if not color then return end getglobal(prefix .. "Name"):SetTextColor(color.r, color.g, color.b) getglobal(prefix .. "Class"):SetTextColor(color.r, color.g, color.b) getglobal(prefix .. "Level"):SetTextColor(color.r, color.g, color.b) end
-- Ref l.178-181 / l.183-215: the two per-unit repaints. These exist so a level ding or a -- death does NOT go through `RAID_ROSTER_UPDATE` — a 40-row rebuild per point of damage -- taken is what firing the roster event on health would cost. function RaidGroupFrame_UpdateLevel(id) getglobal("RaidGroupButton" .. id .. "Level"):SetText(UnitLevel("raid" .. id)) end
function RaidGroupFrame_UpdateHealth(id) local button = getglobal("RaidGroupButton" .. id) local name, rank, subgroup, level, class, fileName, zone, online, isDead = GetRaidRosterInfo(id) RaidGroupButton_SetRowColor(button, fileName, online, isDead) end
-- The `raidN` token → its row index, or nil for anything else. `UNIT_LEVEL`/`UNIT_HEALTH` -- arrive for every unit in the game, so this is also the filter. -- -- `string.find` with a capture rather than `string.match`: this VM is deliberately 5.0 -- (decision 1194), and `string.match` is one of the 5.1-only members that layer REMOVES — -- calling it here would be the same mistake the addons that branch on `gmatch or gfind` -- catch us in. The reference spells the same test as `gsub("raid([0-9]+)", "%1")` and -- reads its substitution count; a capture says it once. local function raid_index_of(unit) if not unit then return nil end local _, _, digits = string.find(unit, "^raid(%d+)$") return tonumber(digits) end
function RaidGroupFrame_OnEvent(event, unit) RaidFrame_OnEvent(event) if event == "UNIT_LEVEL" or event == "UNIT_HEALTH" then local id = raid_index_of(unit) -- Only a row that is actually on screen: an index past the roster names a hidden -- button whose FontStrings still exist, and writing to it would be invisible work. if id and id <= GetNumRaidMembers() then if event == "UNIT_LEVEL" then RaidGroupFrame_UpdateLevel(id) else RaidGroupFrame_UpdateHealth(id) end end end if event == "PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD" then RaidFrameReadyCheckButton_Update() RaidFrameAddMemberButton_Update() end end
-- Ref l.17-22: a drag in flight when the pane closes is a drag that has to be finished, -- or the row stays parked under a cursor that is no longer over anything. function RaidGroupFrame_OnHide() if MOVING_RAID_MEMBER then RaidGroupButton_OnDragStop(MOVING_RAID_MEMBER) end end
-- ── The drag (ref l.217-272) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- -- Hover detection is a per-frame sweep of all 40 slots rather than the slots' own -- OnEnter/OnLeave, and that is the reference's design for a reason worth keeping: the row -- being dragged sits UNDER the cursor, so it — not the slot — is what the pointer is over, -- and no slot would ever get an OnEnter. function RaidGroupFrame_OnUpdate() if not MOVING_RAID_MEMBER then return end TARGET_RAID_SLOT = nil for i = 1, NUM_RAID_GROUPS do for j = 1, MEMBERS_PER_RAID_GROUP do local slot = getglobal("RaidGroup" .. i .. "Slot" .. j) if MouseIsOver(slot) then slot:LockHighlight() TARGET_RAID_SLOT = slot else slot:UnlockHighlight() end end end end
function RaidGroupButton_OnDragStart() -- Leader-only, ref l.234. A non-leader's drag never starts, so there is nothing to -- cancel and nothing to send. if not IsRaidLeader() then return end local cursorX, cursorY = GetCursorPosition() this:ClearAllPoints() -- The ref multiplies the cursor by `GetScreenWidthScale()`/`GetScreenHeightScale()` -- here because 1.12 hands Lua screen pixels against a 1024x768 reference UI. benilla's -- UI space is 1:1 logical px and `GetCursorPosition` already reports in the space -- `SetPoint` offsets are read in, so the multiply would place the row at ~1.5x the -- cursor on a 1600-wide window. Same divergence UIParent.xml's `MouseIsOver` records -- for `GetEffectiveScale`; the two scale getters exist there for the addons that call -- them. this:SetPoint("CENTER", "UIParent", "BOTTOMLEFT", cursorX, cursorY) this:StartMoving() MOVING_RAID_MEMBER = this SetRaidRosterSelection(this.id) end
function RaidGroupButton_OnDragStop(raidButton) if not IsRaidLeader() then return end raidButton = raidButton or this raidButton:StopMovingOrSizing() MOVING_RAID_MEMBER = nil
-- Three landings, ref l.256-272. Dropped on another group's slot: SWAP if somebody is -- in it, MOVE if it is empty. Dropped anywhere else — including this row's own group — -- the row springs back to the slot it came from and nothing goes on the wire. local slot = TARGET_RAID_SLOT if slot then slot:UnlockHighlight() end if slot and slot:GetParent():GetID() ~= raidButton.subgroup then if slot.button then SwapRaidSubgroup(raidButton:GetID(), getglobal(slot.button):GetID()) else -- Seat it optimistically in the target group's next free slot so the row does -- not visibly snap home and back while the server's echo is in flight. local parent = slot:GetParent() raidButton:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", parent:GetName() .. "Slot" .. parent.nextIndex, "TOPLEFT", 0, 0) SetRaidSubgroup(raidButton:GetID(), parent:GetID()) end else raidButton:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", raidButton.slot, "TOPLEFT", 0, 0) end TARGET_RAID_SLOT = nil end
-- ── The row's click and hover (ref l.274-311) ─────────────────────────────────────────── function RaidGroupButton_OnClick(button) if button == "LeftButton" then local unit = "raid" .. this.id if SpellIsTargeting() then SpellTargetUnit(unit) elseif CursorHasItem() then DropItemOnUnit(unit) else TargetUnit(unit) end else HideDropDownMenu(1) if this.id and this.name then BenillaRaidDropDown.initialize = RaidFrameDropDown_Initialize BenillaRaidDropDown.displayMode = "MENU" BenillaRaidDropDown.unit = this.unit BenillaRaidDropDown.rowName = this.name BenillaRaidDropDown.rowId = this.id ToggleDropDownMenu(1, nil, BenillaRaidDropDown, "cursor") end end end
-- The RAID menu's fourth argument is the ROW INDEX, and it is load-bearing rather than -- decorative: every one of the menu's four rows re-reads `GetRaidRosterInfo(userData)` to -- decide whether to show itself, and `UninviteFromRaid` acts on it directly. function RaidFrameDropDown_Initialize() UnitPopup_ShowMenu(getglobal(UIDROPDOWNMENU_OPEN_MENU), "RAID", BenillaRaidDropDown.unit, BenillaRaidDropDown.rowName, BenillaRaidDropDown.rowId) end
function RaidGroupButton_OnEnter() if SpellIsTargeting() then if SpellCanTargetUnit(this.unit) then SetCursor("CAST_CURSOR") else SetCursor("CAST_ERROR_CURSOR") end end GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, this) if GameTooltip:SetUnit(this.unit) then getglobal("GameTooltipTextLeft1"):SetTextColor(GameTooltip_UnitColor(this.unit)) end end
-- Ref l.393-399: every slot forgets its occupant before a repaint re-seats them, so a -- member who left does not leave a stale name behind for the drop code to swap with. function RaidGroup_ResetSlotButtons() for i = 1, NUM_RAID_GROUPS do for j = 1, MEMBERS_PER_RAID_GROUP do getglobal("RaidGroup" .. i .. "Slot" .. j).button = nil end end end
-- ── The two managing buttons (ref l.646-668) ──────────────────────────────────────────── function RaidFrameReadyCheckButton_Update() set_shown(RaidFrameReadyCheckButton, GetNumRaidMembers() > 0 and IsRaidLeader()) end
function RaidFrameAddMemberButton_Update() local inRaid = GetNumRaidMembers() > 0 set_shown(RaidFrameAddMemberButton, inRaid) if inRaid then -- Ref l.662-666. `IsRaidOfficer()` answers nil in benilla today — the binding's -- own body has not been carved (`0x4bb910`, and `script/party.rs` carries why -- guessing it was refused), so an ASSISTANT sees this button disabled where the -- reference enables it. Stated rather than papered over: the leader half is exact, -- and the day that binding lands this line is already right. set_enabled(RaidFrameAddMemberButton, IsRaidLeader() or IsRaidOfficer()) end end
-- ── The saved-instance panel (ref RaidFrame.lua RaidInfoFrame_Update l.90-115) ────────── function RaidInfoFrame_Update() local savedInstances = GetNumSavedInstances() for i = 1, MAX_RAID_INFOS do local row = getglobal("RaidInfoInstance" .. i) if i <= savedInstances then local instanceName, instanceID, instanceReset = GetSavedInstanceInfo(i) getglobal("RaidInfoInstance" .. i .. "Name"):SetText(instanceName) getglobal("RaidInfoInstance" .. i .. "ID"):SetText(instanceID) getglobal("RaidInfoInstance" .. i .. "Reset"):SetText( RESETS_IN .. " " .. SecondsToTime(instanceReset)) row:Show() else row:Hide() end end -- Ref l.108-113: four rows fit, so the bar appears at five. Unlike the reference this -- runs on the empty case too — its early `if ( savedInstances > 0 )` leaves a stale -- scroll bar standing when the last lockout expires, which is a bug rather than a -- behaviour (nothing can observe the bar's absence except by seeing it wrongly there). local scrollable = savedInstances > 4 set_shown(RaidInfoScrollFrameScrollBar, scrollable) if scrollable then -- **The bar has to move to the trough.** `UIPanelScrollFrameTemplate` seats it for -- a bare ScrollFrame: 6 px out and 16 px down, so its up-arrow fits inside the -- frame's own span. This panel draws an ornate trough behind it instead -- (`RaidInfoScrollFrameTop`/`Bottom`, 30 px wide from +1), and the template's seat -- leaves the 16-wide bar 2 px left of that trough's centre with its arrow floating -- 13 px below the cap. The ref re-points it here for the same reason and never -- puts it back — the value never varies, so setting it on each show is idempotent. RaidInfoScrollFrameScrollBar:SetPoint( "TOPLEFT", "RaidInfoScrollFrame", "TOPRIGHT", 8, -3) end RaidInfoScrollFrame:UpdateScrollChildRect() end
-- ── The ready check (ref Blizzard_RaidUI.lua l.615-645) ───────────────────────────────── -- -- Opened by UIParent's `READY_CHECK` arm — the engine event (`0x218`) the -- `MSG_RAID_READY_CHECK` handler fires. The 30 s deadline is the reference's own -- (`0xb713f4 = clock + 0x7530`, wow-re `system/ui/ui.md`); it lives in the frame's -- OnUpdate here because that is where the reference keeps it too. function ShowReadyCheck() local name, leader for i = 1, MAX_RAID_MEMBERS do local rowName, rank = GetRaidRosterInfo(i) if rowName then name = rowName if rank == 2 then leader = "raid" .. i break end end end -- The ref passes `leader` to SetPortraitTexture unguarded and would take a nil there -- if no rank-2 row existed; ours does not, because a raid whose leader is out of the -- roster (the moment after a promote, before the echo) is reachable and a raise in an -- event handler is a script error the player sees. if leader then SetPortraitTexture(ReadyCheckPortrait, leader) end ReadyCheckFrameText:SetText(format(READY_CHECK_MESSAGE, name or UNKNOWN)) ReadyCheckFrame:Show() ReadyCheckFrame.timer = 30 PlaySound("ReadyCheck") end
function ReadyCheck_OnUpdate(elapsed) if not ReadyCheckFrame.timer then return end ReadyCheckFrame.timer = ReadyCheckFrame.timer - elapsed if ReadyCheckFrame.timer < 0 then -- Timing out is an answer too: you were away, and the raid is told so. local info = ChatTypeInfo["SYSTEM"] DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME:AddMessage(READY_CHECK_YOU_WERE_AFK, info.r, info.g, info.b, info.id) ReadyCheckFrame.timer = nil ReadyCheckFrame:Hide() end end
-- ── Add Member's dialog (ref StaticPopup.lua l.871-895) ───────────────────────────────── StaticPopupDialogs["ADD_RAIDMEMBER"] = { text = ADD_RAIDMEMBER_LABEL, button1 = "Accept", button2 = "Cancel", hasEditBox = 1, maxLetters = 12, timeout = 0, hideOnEscape = 1, OnAccept = function() InviteByName(getglobal("StaticPopup1EditBox"):GetText()) end, OnShow = function() getglobal("StaticPopup1EditBox"):SetFocus() end, EditBoxOnEnterPressed = function() InviteByName(getglobal("StaticPopup1EditBox"):GetText()) StaticPopup_Hide("ADD_RAIDMEMBER") end, }

Scripts.OnClick: if UnitCanCooperate("player", "target") then InviteByName(UnitName("target")) else StaticPopup_Show("ADD_RAIDMEMBER") end
if RaidInfoFrame:IsShown() then RaidInfoFrame:Hide() else RaidInfoFrame:Show() end

Scripts.OnEvent: -- The raid ending ends the question with it. if event == "RAID_ROSTER_UPDATE" and GetNumRaidMembers() == 0 then ReadyCheckFrame.timer = nil ReadyCheckFrame:Hide() end
